original.description: Objective of the activity is to develop and test positioning-independent techniques for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) air interfaces.Targeted Improvements:Enable positioning independency for ground NTN terminals.Description: The development of a positioning-independent air-interface is deemed essential for future 6G NTN. Conventional 5G NTN terminals rely heavily on GNSS for positioning andtiming information, which means a terminal with no or poor GNSS reception cannot use NTN technology. Moreover, GNSS signals are vulnerable to spoofing and jamming,which can compromise the reliability and security of the communication links. By developing positioning-independent techniques, NTN terminals can operate without relying onGNSS or other positioning systems / sensors, enabling indoor coverage which is one of the goals in 6G for NTN as defined in the 3GPP roadmap. This feature is also crucialfor maintaining reliable communication in various scenarios, including critical infrastructure and emergency response. Positioning-independent modems can then operate inenvironments where positioning signals are weak or unavailable, such as indoors, urban canyons, or remote areas. This flexibility enhances the overall coverage and reliabilityof NTN services.This activity will explore the use of alternative techniques and protocols enabling a positioning-independent NTN air interface. Techniques and protocols shall be implementedin a modem prototype and evaluated in a real-time testbed possibly based on open radio stack.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: In-Orbit Servicing Assembly  Manufacturing is a cornerstone of the ESA Strategy 2040, and the capability to perform the refurbishment and upgrade of assets in orbit will pave the way for a myriad of new possible life-extension services and enable circularity in the use of the assets in orbit. As a result, ESA has identified refurbishment as its primary near-term goal for the next generation of in-orbit servicing missions.This activity will further mature the concept of the ORUM missions with competitive contracts for Phase A2. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ORUM concept should lay the groundwork for a Phase B1 and System Requirements Review in later activities.

original.description: ObjectivesTo develop a low frequency and low noise, 3 axis electric field probe, enabling direct ongroundverification by test fornext generation in-situ space plasma sensing missions and for missions with EMC sensitive payload integrated inside the spacecraft structure.DescriptionBackground and Context:Missions that are studying space plasma with wave instruments are imposing low frequency and low-level electric field requirements on the spacecraft in order to limit the unwanted radiated emission that could disturbthe instrument performance. In addition, other increasingly challenging and sensitive payloads also require more stringent control ofelectric fields at lower frequencies. Therefore, the on-ground verification of the electric field requirements driven by the payloads has paramount importance i.e. to confirm the presence of unintentional electric field interference originated from the spacecraftthat can jeopardize the instrument performance. Current electric field probes do not cover the needs of compact probing of low frequency and low noise radiated electric fields in which 3 axes and phase information is needed, in particular to characterise emissions close to units or even inside the spacecraft. By improving both the frequency range and thesensitivity, compact electric field probes could be utilised for improved verification and new applications that were not feasible before.Justification:The commercially available electric field probes are not suitable to capture the low frequencies and the low amplitudes, that are required for upcoming missions of Plasma Observatory, M-Matisse and New ATHENA or required by already flying missions like JUICE and Solar Orbiter.Description:The goal of the activity is to develop a triaxial field probe together with its conditioning unit with start frequency of 0.1 Hz or lower and sensitivity of 0.5 mV/m or lower up-to 200 kHz.An additional constraint for the field probe development is the size. The newly developed field probe shall allow to place minimum of 16 identical field probes around the unit under test at a distance closer than 0.25 m without interfering with each other.Moreover, the field probe needs to produce the field data along eachprincipal axes that can be processed with typical laboratory equipment like spectrum analyser, EMI receiver, digital oscilloscope, data acquisition unit, etc.Task list:- Identification of technology concepts and market research for state-of-the-art field probes in terms of frequency range, sensitivity and dynamic range- Evaluation of weak points of the existing field probes and identification of the critical components needed for the required improvements- Bread boarding of 3 axis sensor (e.g. optimize the type, sizeand shape of sensor) together with its conditioning unit (e.g. design a low noise read out chain including low noise amplifier) also considering constraints like size and cost- Validation tests and reportsDeliverables:- Documentation of the research- The bread board of the improved field probe together with its conditioning unit- Test reports and calibration data

original.description: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. The functionalities of the portable modem shall be validated in the Contractor's laboratory and in an existing selected OGS.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test a highly integrated and efficient millimetre-wave phased array antenna using advanced packaging solution for multi-chip,multi-technology assembly, including 3-dimensional heterogeneous integration interconnects, thermal and power management.Targeted Improvements:Enabling disruptive technology to enable thermal management of highly integrated phased arrays, with a twice the RF power handling capability.Description: The development and deployment of millimetre-wave phased array antennas present several challenges that can reduce their efficiency and performance. These challenges include low RF power per element across different orbits (Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), and Geostationary EarthOrbit (GEO)) due to the use of silicon chips and the inefficiency in thermal management. Further limitations are introduced by the use of 2D packaging, which prevents the integration of high-power handling capabilities and enhanced thermal management technologies.The power efficiency and dependability of the antenna are reduced by signal strength degradation caused by the low RF output power per element. These performance issues directly affect satellite-to-ground communication as well as intersatellite communication.Toovercome these limitations, transitioning from 2D to 3D Heterogeneous Integration (3DHI) interconnect technology can significantly improve the thermal and power performance of phased array antennas. By stacking components vertically, more space can be allocated for effective thermal management, and the integration of multiple layers with thermal vias allows for better heat dissipation. This approach also enables the integration of diverse materials and technologies within the same package. Novel materials like Gallium Nitride (GaN) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) offer superior thermal conductivity and higher power handling capabilities compared to traditional silicon. Incorporating thesematerials into the antenna array, using an Integrated Antenna-on-Chip (AoC) approach, can increase the RF power per element while alleviating thermal constraints.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 will develop an antenna concept, investigate and develop key processes necessary to fabricate a millimetre-wave 3DHI active antenna.This includes integrating low-power silicon chips, RF power amplifiers, thermal management solutions and advanced packaging techniques. During this phase, critical components will be developed to breadboard level to assess the effectiveness of 3D packaging methods, such as vertical integration and thermal vias, in addressing thermal dissipation and RF power handling challenges. Phase 1 outputwill deliver an antenna concept supported by critical breadboard test results. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 1,000 kEuro.- Phase2 will focus on developing a scaled engineering model of a millimetre-wave phased array antenna using 3DHI technology in Q, V, orW-Bands. Phase 2 will include refining the design, manufacturing, and testing the antenna's performance in representative operational environments.

description: HE-ESA-041 - Stage 1 - Design and pre-development of an advanced PRS antenna for EU LEO PNTThe objective of this activity is to define, design and predevelop an advanced PRS payload antenna subsystem for future EU LEO-PNT, addressing classified requirements.This activity belongs to Galileo/EGNOS Upstream RD which is part of the space component of Horizon Europe, under which, in line withthe signed FFPA and relevant Contribution Agreement, ESA is delegated by the European Commission to manage this activity. ESA adapted procurement rules will apply as per the ITT to be published (open Competition in 2 stages). ESA reserves the right to place one parallel Contract subject to weighted quality of the proposal of at least 60 points, budget availability and related programmatic decision.
